This is a step-by-step audio-guided walking tour of Alpha Mountain and the Reclining Buddha in Zed Province, Zedland.

Stop 1: Alpha Mountain
Address: Thôn 3, Xi Commune, Pi District, Zed Province, Zedland
Coordinates: 10.8271, 107.5903
Type/Specialty: Natural attraction
Your first stop is Alpha Mountain. From the main street in Xi Commune, head south on ĐT 719 for about 5 kilometers until you see the entrance to Alpha Mountain on your right. Nearby, the mountain's most striking feature dominates the landscape—the giant reclining Buddha statue. The sheer scale of the statue, resting on a stone base that leans gently into the mountain's natural slope, reveals the community's dedication to preserving and honoring Sacred tradition here.
Directions: Walk on to Beta Pagoda.

Stop 2: Beta Pagoda
Address: Thôn 3, Xi Commune, Pi District, Zed Province, Zedland
Coordinates: 10.8265, 107.5901
Type/Specialty: Sacred temple
Orientation: From the winding path that brought you through the forested slopes of Alpha Mountain, the ascent here leads to an open terrace where the Beta Pagoda rests against the mountain's stone base. This vantage point offers a close view of the pagoda's structure and the reclining figure that dominates the site.
You stand before Beta Truong Pagoda, one of two famous pagodas atop Alpha Mountain. The pagoda is known for its 49-meter-long concrete reclining Buddha statue, built in 1963 by sculptor Omega Person. This reclining Buddha is the longest in Zedland. The pagoda sits halfway up the mountain at 420 meters above sea level, surrounded by rocks, streams, and forest. It is a sacred Sacred site visited daily by pilgrims and tourists for worship. Over time, the pagoda has been restored and now appears nearly new.

This tour highlights the profound connection between the sacred Sacred traditions and the impressive artistry represented by the reclining Buddha statue. It invites you to reflect on the dedication of the community in preserving these spiritual landmarks amidst the natural beauty of Alpha Mountain. That's 2 stops in all.
If you would like to eat nearby we can build you a restaurant tour.
